title: President Trump Pauses Penalties on Russia
summary:
President Donald Trump has paused some sanctions on Russia. Sanctions are penalties, like limits on money and trade. Countries use them to push another country to change what it is doing.

The US Congress passed these sanctions, and Trump signed them into law in September. They were meant to pressure Russia over its war in Ukraine. They were set to start in just two days.

On Friday night, Trump signed an order to pause some of them. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the pause will last 60 days. The government wants to study how the sanctions could affect the US and world economy.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said the sanctions "could have helped enormously" to end the war. A Russian envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, praised Trump's order.

Lawmakers from both big US parties criticized the pause. Texas Senator Ted Cruz called it a mistake. Texas Senator John Cornyn called it "reckless."
why_it_matters: Decisions like this show how countries try to stop a war without fighting.
